C.O.R.A.L. (Computational Observation and Real-time Astronaut Life-monitoring) is an interdisciplinary team blending computer science and industrial design. We create intuitive, user-centered solutions that turn complex astronaut health data into accessible experiences for space missions.

Every Signal Matters. Every Life Counts.

Beyond physical health monitoring, C.O.R.A.L. addresses the psychological challenges of space exploration, particularly isolation, loneliness, and separation from Earth. It integrates vital signs, daily health assessments, vision and hearing tests, balance screening, sleep, mood, and exercise monitoring into one unified platform.
Through personalized feedback and early alerts, C.O.R.A.L. supports astronauts' physical and emotional well-being in environments with limited access to medical and psychological support.
details:
C.O.R.A.L

C.O.R.A.L (Computational Observation and Real-time Astronaut Life-monitoring) is a human-centered health monitoring system concept designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions.

The platform brings physical health monitoring and psychological well-being together in one integrated interface. It includes daily health check-ins, vital sign monitoring, vision and hearing assessments, balance tests, sleep and mood tracking, and exercise and nutrition monitoring. These features help astronauts monitor changes in their health and maintain awareness of their overall well-being.

To make daily health monitoring more engaging, C.O.R.A.L. incorporates interactive and game-based assessments. Tests such as balance, vision, and hearing evaluations are designed as short interactive activities that encourage astronaut participation and make routine health check-ins less repetitive. This approach aims to improve engagement and support consistent self-monitoring throughout the mission.

A key focus of C.O.R.A.L. is addressing the psychological effects of isolation and separation from Earth. Its dedicated HOPE section is designed to strengthen astronauts' emotional connection with home. Astronauts can select up to three personally meaningful locations on Earth, which are displayed within the application as familiar visual connections to their lives back home. Additionally, selected individuals, such as family members and close friends, can send personal messages that astronauts can access through the HOPE menu. This feature aims to provide emotional comfort and reduce feelings of loneliness during extended missions.

The platform also incorporates personalized feedback, early health alerts, and an intelligent assistant concept to create a more supportive and engaging monitoring experience. Emergency guidance is also considered for situations where communication with Earth is limited or unavailable.

The project follows a human-centered design approach, considering microgravity, radiation exposure, physical changes, psychological stress, limited medical access, and the challenges of living in confined environments. Its interface is designed to make health information accessible, understandable, and easy to navigate during demanding missions.

C.O.R.A.L. was developed as an interactive software prototype using Figma, with a focus on user interface design, user experience, and interactive prototyping. The concept also envisions future integration with wearable devices and health sensors to collect real-time physiological data.

Our goal is to move beyond conventional health tracking and create a more comprehensive approach to astronaut care, where both physical health and emotional well-being matter.
